experiment: P1: V2 Firefox WASM Latency Fix — COOP/COEP runtime fix (numThreads tuning trialled + reverted)
mission: Next Mission — Productionize the V2 Firefox WASM Fix

artifact.status: FP32 canonical — UNCHANGED. INT8 candidate NOT applied (out of scope; original preserved byte-for-byte).

environment.methodology: real production path via /staging-harness.html → window.__stagingTest.runLatencyBenchmark → embedEEG() → ONNXAdapter → defaultRuntime() → verifyRemoteArtifact (crypto.subtle.digest) → InferenceSession.create + run + unload. per-call session (matches T-035 + production embedEEG).

dev_layers: vite-plugins/test-harness.ts → setCoopHeaders() at harness-HTML + /ort/*.wasm + /ort/*.mjs?import res.end sites (these bypass Vite's headers middleware via prepended res.end)
fix.prod_layer: src/server.ts → withCrossOriginIsolationHeaders() on every SSR/static Response

experiments.gate: FAIL (P95<600 NOT met). Deferred to INT8-QDQ ablation (P2, out of scope this mission). Regression floor <2500 enforced in test.
experiments.conclusion: Cross-origin isolation + SAB verified; latency remains single-threaded ORT WASM (~1.6s). Not a COOP/COEP problem — ORT-Web defaults numThreads=1; threading per-session was negative.

NEGATIVE result (recorded, not committed as a fix). embedEEG() creates a fresh InferenceSession per call (embed() → createAdapter → load → unload in finally), so numThreads>1 forces a new Web Worker thread-pool to spin up AND tear down on every call; worker spin-up dominates the tiny V2 compute → Firefox P95 1742→2658ms. Threading only helps with a REUSED session/thread-pool, which the per-request embedEEG() path does not provide. Setting reverted; onnx-adapter.ts restored to original (numThreads left at ORT-Web default 1).
experiments.action_taken: Reverted defaultRuntime() numThreads change (onnx-adapter.ts back to wasmPaths-only).

decision_detail: The permanent COOP/COEP runtime fix is implemented and verified in the real application (crossOriginIsolated===true, SharedArrayBuffer available, on both Chromium and Firefox). Correctness gates (real V2 inference, 0 fallbacks, dim=32, SHA-256 verified, determinism cos=1.0) and the Chromium latency gate (P95 530ms) PASS. The Firefox latency gate (<600ms) is NOT cleared by COOP/COEP + numThreads tuning: ORT-Web defaults numThreads=1, and per-session thread-pool spin-up (required because embedEEG() creates a fresh session per call) is a negative lever. Clearing the Firefox gate requires the INT8-QDQ ablation (smaller model + INT8 kernels), which is explicitly out of scope for this mission ('do not replace V2 with INT8 yet').
next_mission_recommendation: INT8-QDQ V2 ablation (offline CPU parity + size via onnxruntime.quantization, then browser latency/accuracy on Chromium+Firefox, preserving the FP32 canonical artifact) AND evaluate persistent InferenceSession + thread-pool reuse across embedEEG() calls to amortise worker spin-up.
